subdomain: 5.4 Ensure compliance with regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA, FedRAMP)

en.question: A supplier promises not to use a company's API content for model training without permission. The project team wants to describe the entire assistant as retaining no customer data, although it has not checked feature storage, third-party tools, or application logs. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: Separate training use from retention; verify actual deployment terms, feature storage, third-party tools, and company logs before claiming zero storage.
options.note: A no-training commitment does not establish that content is never stored. Retention obligations and evidence must cover the actual data paths, including those outside the model provider.

options.text: The no-training promise establishes zero retention for prompts and responses, so only the company's application logs need further review.
options.note: Provider features can require storage without using the data for training. Excluding those paths would leave the proposed zero-retention claim unsupported.

options.text: A successful API response demonstrates that the request met every applicable retention arrangement, so additional feature-level verification is unnecessary.
options.note: Request acceptance is not an end-to-end retention attestation. Some arrangements and external integrations require checks that an ordinary API success does not perform.

options.text: Encrypted storage can be treated as nonretention, so the team may make the claim if every service promises encryption at rest.
options.note: Encryption protects stored data but does not make the storage disappear. Retention duration, access, deletion, and arrangement scope remain separate questions.

references.title: Anthropic Privacy Center: How long do you store my organization's data?
